CPC overtime fraud case: Ananda Palitha further remanded

cards.what_happened: D.D. Ananda Palitha, convenor of the Samagi Joint Trade Union Alliance, has been further remanded until December 4 over an alleged Rs. 3.1 million overtime allowance fraud at the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation. Colombo Additional Magistrate Liyan Warusha Vithana issued the order today (25) after submissions by the Central Crime Investigation Bureau. Palitha was arrested by the bureau on November 16.
details: The case concerns alleged misappropriation of employee overtime allowances at the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC). Investigating officers told the court that the alleged fraud involved Rs. 3.1 million and took place over a five-year period from 2015 to 2019. Palitha is the convenor of the Samagi Joint Trade Union Alliance.

Colombo Additional Magistrate Liyan Warusha Vithana ordered the further remand until December 4. The order was made today (25) after submissions by the Central Crime Investigation Bureau. Palitha was arrested by the Central Crime Investigation Bureau on November 16 in connection with the investigation.

Arrest warrant issued for Rajangane Saddharathana over failure to appear in court

cards.what_happened: The Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court issued an arrest warrant for Rajangane Saddharathana on the 25 after he failed to appear in court. The case involves alleged social media statements said to be detrimental to religious harmony. Magistrate Pasan Amarasena also ordered notices to be issued to his bail sureties.
details: According to Newswire, the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court issued the warrant on the 25 because Rajangane Saddharathana did not appear before the court. The case concerns alleged statements on social media that were said to harm religious harmony. Magistrate Pasan Amarasena made the order.

The court acted after receiving submissions from the Criminal Investigation Department. It also ordered that notices be issued to Saddharathana's bail sureties. The case has been adjourned to February 24, 2027, for the Government Analyst's reports to be submitted.

Saddharathana was expelled from the Buddhist monastic order. He had earlier been arrested by the CID over the alleged controversial statements and was released on bail. He is now in remand custody over a separate case linked to the tense situation at the sacred city of Anuradhapura.

He failed to appear in a case about alleged social media statements harmful to religious harmony.
Magistrate Pasan Amarasena ordered notices to his bail sureties after CID submissions.
The case will be heard again on February 24, 2027, for Government Analyst's reports.
Saddharathana was expelled from the Buddhist monastic order.
He was previously arrested by the CID and released on bail.
He is in remand custody over a separate case involving the sacred city of Anuradhapura.

The Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court made the order on the 25 because he did not show up for a case involving alleged social media statements said to harm religious harmony. Magistrate Pasan Amarasena also ordered notices to be issued to his bail sureties, acting on submissions from the Criminal Investigation Department. The case is set to return on February 24, 2027, so the Government Analyst's reports can be submitted. Saddharathana was expelled from the Buddhist monastic order and had been arrested before by the CID over the same alleged statements, though he was released on bail. Right now he is in remand custody over a separate case tied to the tense situation at the sacred city of Anuradhapura.

sri_lanka.title: Illegal vehicle possession: Johnston fined Rs. 130,000, handed suspended sentence

cards.what_happened: Former Minister Johnston Fernando was fined a total of Rs. 130,000 and given a six-month suspended prison sentence by the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court today (25) for illegally possessing a vehicle.
details: Former Minister Johnston Fernando appeared at the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court today (25) in a case about the illegal possession of a vehicle. The court found him guilty and imposed a total fine of Rs. 130,000 along with a six-month suspended prison sentence.

On the first charge, he was fined Rs. 5,000, with a three-month prison sentence if he does not pay. On the second charge, Fernando was fined Rs. 100,000 and sentenced to six months of simple imprisonment, suspended for five years.
On the third charge, the court fined him Rs. 25,000, with a three-month sentence of simple imprisonment in default of payment. The verdict and all penalties were reported by Newswire.
key_facts: Former Minister Johnston Fernando fined Rs. 130,000 total by the court.
Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court gave a six-month suspended sentence today (25).
The case involved the illegal possession of a vehicle.
First charge: Rs. 5,000 fine, three months in prison if unpaid.
Second charge: Rs. 100,000 fine, six months suspended for five years.
Third charge: Rs. 25,000 fine, three months in prison if unpaid.
The report comes from Newswire.
cards.blurb: Former Minister Johnston Fernando fined Rs. 130,000 and given a suspended sentence for illegal vehicle possession.
cards.spoken: Hello and welcome to the news. A former minister named Johnston Fernando has been sentenced by the Colombo Fort Magistrate's Court. The case was about the illegal possession of a vehicle, and the verdict came out today (25). The court fined him a total of Rs. 130,000 and gave him a six month suspended prison sentence. For the first charge, he must pay Rs. 5,000 or spend three months in prison. For the second charge, he was fined Rs. 100,000 and sentenced to six months of simple imprisonment, suspended for five years. For the third charge, the fine is Rs. 25,000, with three months of simple imprisonment if he does not pay. This report is from Newswire.
